name: Ulnar Hypoplasia-Split Foot Syndrome
aliases: Ulnar Ray Deficiency with Split Foot

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Ulnar Hypoplasia-Split Foot Syndrome

criteria.description: Hypoplasia or aplasia of the ulnar bone and associated structures
Presence of split foot (ectrodactyly) with median cleft and missing central rays
Radiographic evidence of ulnar ray deficiency and split foot malformation
Positive family history suggestive of autosomal dominant or sporadic occurrence
Exclusion of other syndromes with limb malformations

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ulnar hypoplasia and split foot deformity confirmed clinically and radiologically
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing may aid but is not definitive.

imaging: Radiographs showing hypoplasia or aplasia of the ulna
Radiographs demonstrating split foot deformity with median cleft
MRI may show soft tissue hypoplasia in affected limb
genetic: Possible mutations in genes involved in limb development (e.g., TP63 gene variants reported in some cases)
Genetic testing may be inconclusive due to heterogeneity
other: Clinical examination revealing limb asymmetry and digital anomalies

distinguishingFeatures: More prominent central ray absence in both hands and feet
Often familial with autosomal dominant inheritance
Distinct facial features absent in ulnar hypoplasia-split foot syndrome

redFlags: Severe functional impairment of the hand
Progressive limb deformity or worsening contractures
references: Orphanet: Ulnar Hypoplasia-Split Foot Syndrome - ORPHA:1122
